main_body: Green sofa drawn straight from the front: a light backrest panel (rows 1-5), a dark band (rows 6-7), a lighter seat cushion band (rows 8-11), a dark front base (rows 12-13), an outline row 14 and two small legs.
top_band: No clear top surface. Row 1 is a 1-row light highlight, rows 2-5 are the backrest face, and rows 8-11 are a light cushion band with a centre divider that reads as a vertical front face.
evidence: Everything is stacked horizontal bands seen face-on: backrest, shadow, cushion, base. The seat cushion is a short light strip (the 4 rows at 8-11 include a highlight row 8 and a highlight row 11) with a vertical seam at x=19 rows 8-10. It does not read as a foreshortened horizontal seat surface seen from above. There is no front-edge step or overhang shadow separating a top from the front. The scan shows the same repeating light/dark pattern in all three columns. This is a front elevation, and the seat surface is not seen from above.

style.evidence: The sofa uses only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile, against 17-20 per tile and 38-40 colours in the references. The surfaces are flat bands with no grain, stitching, fabric texture or per-cushion shading. The outline is a dark green tone (0% neutral), which is fine. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage figure is 0%, but only because the bands are thin; the bands themselves are one flat colour. The piece is much flatter and thinner than the Beodeul references.
